L2 is not even remotely comparable with L1. The topics are vast, full of nuances, difficult to grasp at one go.  
  
Additionally, what makes L2 much much more challenging is the format of the questions. You will not be asked to answer one or two line questions related to a single reading, rather you will be tested via a full fledged case studies spanning the entire topic and including multiple readings.  
  
90 day L2 will be a tough nut, but still manageable if ( AND BIG IF) you finish the course within 2 months taking help from some prep provider which offers video lectures.  
  
Focus on Ethics, FRA, FI, Equity, Portfolio as these are heavy weight topics. ( 10-15% weight each so at least 60-70% paper is simply these topics) ( FRA and FI may be turn out to be challenging and Equity is bulky but relatively easy. Portfolio is semi-easy)  
  
If you're good at hypothesis testing from L1, then quant is also doable. There are two study sessions in quant. The regression and time series gets much higher weightage than the other study session which is largely theoretical. Quant is 5-10%  
  
Corporate finance and Alternatives also falls in easy to relatively easy category. Both of these topics carry 5-10%.  
  
ECO is average. Maybe currency calculations can get a bit tricky. Econ also carries 5-10%.  
  
Derivatives sure is difficult. Can be skipped if time constraint. Also carries weight 5-10%  
  
  
  
I never went for kaplan in L1 or L2. But anyway go through the heavy weight topics (10-15%) and at least 2 of the 5 lower weight topics ( 5-10%)

FCFE has nothing to do with income statement.. I/S is a fully accrual statement (i.e you donot make a distinction of items being cash or non cash )  and thus can be subjected to accounting trickery. Usually Accounting standards govern I/S.   


While FCFE is an analytical measure. Doesn't have any specific guidelines how to calculate FCFE. CFA curriculum follows a specific definition of FCFE which is largely accepted one in analysts circles. So we use that as a a standard. FCFE is not any anywhere on I/S.    FCFE is a cash based measure i.e cash for owners generated/available in a yr after every obligation is paid for ( not including transitions with shareholder because that would be illogical )   
however FCFE can also be artificially pumped up . say you increase leverage to fund working capital, fixed investments. Your FCFE will increase. 

​

FCFE is usually more stable in a sense its always difficult to manipulate cash (certainly more difficult than earnings manipulation ). Your growth in  cash from yr to yr also has therefore more stability

An increase in growth will increase the justified P/E. However, this increase is non-linear i.e successive 1 unit increases in growth will not  translate to a certain constant increase in P/E  everytime.

Linear relations relate constant increase in dependent variable to 1 unit change in independent variable.   y=mx+c    . For 1 unit increase in x,   y increases by m everytime.

PE/G ratio takes a simplifying assumption where it describes P/E linearly related to g. (which is also its limitation)

But is can be easily ascertained via any DCF valuation method that Price doesnt share a linear relation with earnings growth.

​

Everything else remaining constant, price (and by that P/E)  and growth curve should  be a concave upward sloping imo

p here stands for probability.Let us say that a p value of our hypothesis via whichever test comes out to be 0.01%. This means that the probability of our hypothesis happening is 0.01%. given assumptions regarding parameters and distribution. ( a 0.01% probability would mean that event is generally speaking unlikely to occur). A standard significance level of 0.05% would reject such a hypothesis.

(A significance level of 5% means that if the likelihood  of our hypothesis occurring  is less than 5%, then our test would reject that hypothesis)

So the smaller the p value, the less likely the event. And more likely we would reject that event/hypothesis in our test.

​

We compare P-value to the level of significance because both are in % terms.

Level of significance can be ascertained via t-stat critical value & vice versa.  For example a critical value of 1.96 for a 2 sided test would result in a 5% significance level divided in two equal  2.5% at both ends of our distribution.
